status: exploratory diagnostic specified after viewing the original FX comparisons; freeze before computing these new controls
question: Does native-versus-rolling model ordering also change after a single past-only constant width adjustment?
streams: all 96 saved streams: both contexts, all neural seeds and all classical predictors, each asset separately
frozen_quantile: q is order statistic ceil((n+1)*0.9) of abs(y_i)/s_i from the specified year; h_t=s_t*q without later updates
frozen_is: q minimizes mean interval score in specified year: smallest score r_i=abs(y_i)/s_i whose cumulative s_i weight reaches 0.9 of total s_i weight; no finite-rank correction, no coverage guarantee
objective_note: The ordinary score quantile and scale-weighted IS minimizer solve different objectives; neither is selected using evaluation outcomes.

analysis.units: width and IS divided by each asset's original training-only standard deviation
analysis.aggregation: first average all five fixed neural fits within asset, then equal-weight four assets; classical streams have one fit per asset
analysis.uncertainty: paired circular date blocks, shared across all rules/models/assets; fixed-fit, exploratory, unadjusted, not independent asset/seed evidence
analysis.reporting: retain every rule, context, fit, asset and calendar year; no event selection, best-rule selection, causal explained fraction, or new confirmation claim

decision.if_static_controls_change_order: native-versus-rolling rank reversal alone does not identify temporal-memory dynamics; demand evidence beyond a fixed multiplier
decision.if_static_controls_do_not_change_order: temporal explanation remains a candidate, not established; frozen versus rolling also changes age, sample count and drift exposure
decision.next_gate: only develop a new method after a specific mechanism predicts new controlled outcomes and survives simple controls and fresh evaluation

limitations: The same historical evaluation was already viewed; no new blind holdout.
2019 also selected neural checkpoints, so it is a reused diagnostic sample; 2020 was not used for checkpoint selection.
Both calibration years precede evaluation, but the year choice and controls were specified after original results were known.
A frozen multiplier still multiplies a time-varying predictor; this is not a fixed-width interval.
Different calibration years and rolling windows are not an intervention isolating only dynamics.
Constant scale cancellation and calibration-aware optimization have prior literature; this is a confound check, not a new algorithm.
